review_notes:
I read the whole supplied file, lines 1–142, and checked it against the rubric on repeated proof machinery. I did not open the related source roots or search other Mathlib files for the same pattern. I found two places where the same step occurs twice.

1. `Perfect.small_diam_splitting` applies `small_diam_aux` to `perf0` and to `perf1`. The nontrivial reasoning is already factored into the private lemma `Perfect.small_diam_aux`. What remains is two calls to it and some plumbing for the two outputs, so there is no repeated proof machinery.

2. `Perfect.exists_nat_bool_injection` handles the `false` and `true` cases separately when it builds `DP`, proves `hanti`, proves `hdiam`, and proves `hdisj'`. Each time, the two branches differ only in whether `C0`/`h0` or `C1`/`h1` is used. Each branch is one line (`exact (h0 _ _ _).2.2.1`, `convert (h0 _ _ _).2.2.2`, and so on). The only slightly longer repeated piece is the `convert … ; rw [PiNat.res_length]` step in `hdiam`. The rubric excludes duplicated branches that are merely moved inside a helper, and excludes short routine steps. A Bool-indexed `choose` could shorten these case splits. It would be a stylistic compression, not the extraction of a shared nontrivial argument. I do not count it as a finding.

The last theorem, `IsClosed.exists_nat_bool_injection_of_not_countable`, is a thin wrapper around existing results, with no duplicated reasoning.

I am fairly confident that no finding meets the rubric's bar.
